image.identity_note: Both docker 29 hosts run the containerd image store, whose `docker images` ID is the OCI manifest-list digest. That digest, sha256:237a5025..., is IDENTICAL on the build host and on the endpoint after docker save | docker load, so it is the cross-host identity for this artifact. 49 layers (base 42 + 7 sr1), Size 25078076630.

base.owner_service_digest: sha256:820181fbbc975cd5291c411cda9771d58fecee1636d916f508f47230df20592b (docker.io/voipmonitor/vllm r34 tag pinned by the AIBoss unit; the apc superset is one COPY+RUN above it, docker/Dockerfile.gg-r34-patched-apc)
base.sourced_from: AIBoss podman storage (this rental box holds only the extracted proot rootfs /var/tmp/gg-rootfs, no container runtime)
base.transfer: podman save | zstd -T0 -12 streamed AIBoss -> (jump ns1) -> rental -> driver, 10779120146 bytes in ~26 min (~6.4 MB/s sustained); mid-stream sha256 computed on the rental EQUALS the sha256 of the landed file

identity_across_runtimes.problem: podman's manifest digest (16a936b8...) does not survive podman save | docker load; docker's containerd store re-derives a local manifest digest (driver e6807a61..., endpoint 7141198a... for the SAME tar bytes).
identity_across_runtimes.proof_used_instead: the RootFS diff_id chain (uncompressed layer digests) is runtime-invariant: 42 diff_ids, sha256(JSON list) = 886dbafce1ec07d743e34b9f2150f8fe8f9f9760f5aa857107ae027e1767abc3, IDENTICAL on AIBoss podman, driver docker, endpoint docker. Belt and braces, Containerfile Layer 0 fails the build unless six load-bearing in-image files are byte-identical to the promoted image (shas below).
identity_across_runtimes.from_by_digest_caveat: BuildKit's resolver treats digest refs as registry references (FROM localhost/vllm@sha256:... dials a registry at localhost:443), so the build FROMs the locally loaded name:tag and pins content via the Layer 0 gate instead. Stated, not hidden.

patch_layers.what: Port of vllm-project/vllm#52530 (branch fix/kv-pool-unservable-request-admission @ 479413adc): admission gate in add_request + length cap via check_stop(request, max_servable_num_tokens), so a request no future KV-pool state can hold is failed once instead of retried forever (#52520 livelock)
patch_layers.port_verdict: PORTABLE - the fork's kv_cache_utils.py carries identical helper signatures (_estimate_max_model_len_from_groups, _pool_bytes_per_block, _use_packed_kv_cache_config) and the scheduler is structurally close. Hand-ported, not auto-applied: upstream's scheduler hunks anchor on code the fork lacks (grammar_compile_error_reqs) and on a finish_requests that returns Request objects.
adaptations: THE one behavioural adaptation: the fork's finish_requests returns list[(request_id, client_index)] and frees self.requests entries via _free_request, so the unservable flush in update_from_output captures the Request objects BEFORE calling finish_requests (same order as the fork's own failed-KV-load flush directly above it). Upstream iterates the returned Request objects instead.
unservable_reqs set declared in the same __init__ block as max_servable_num_tokens (fork has no grammar_compile_error_reqs to anchor beside)
get_num_unfinished_requests adds len(self.unservable_reqs) on the fork's pause-state-aware variant
patch_layers.safety_audit: never-scheduled requests are safe through the fork's free path: Request.last_sched_seq defaults 0 <= processed_step_seq so _free_request_blocks frees immediately; both request-queue remove_requests implementations tolerate absent items (filter-based)
